title: Maple leaf motif
subtitle: A five-pointed maple leaf in autumn red or orange, 9 cm
excerpt: The maple leaf motif is worked around a centre spine chain, building the five pointed lobes with increasing stitch heights at the point tips. At 9 cm in DK cotton the recognisable maple silhouette is clear — wider and more starred than the oak. It is used on autumn wreaths, Thanksgiving table runners, and seasonal garments.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 7 (1892), botanical leaf motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet leaf applique section.
heroPrompt: A crochet maple leaf applique in deep red DK cotton with five pointed lobes, 9 cm across, photographed flat on natural linen in soft autumn daylight.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished maple leaf measures 9 cm across the widest point and 8 cm tall in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Maple leaf motif
chartDefinition.caption: Centre spine chain. Five pointed lobes fanning outward: centre lobe at top, two mid lobes angled, two lower lobes at the sides. Each lobe rises to a double-treble tip. Stem at base.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch two steps taller than a treble, made with three yarn overs before insertion. UK double treble equals US treble. Used at the tip of each maple lobe for maximum height.

content.text: at each lobe tip to give the maple's characteristically tall, pointed lobes. Five lobes radiate from the spine chain: the centre lobe at the tip, two mid lobes at approximately 45 degrees, and two lower lobes nearly horizontal. The varying angles of the lobes are achieved by working more or fewer slip stitches between lobe bases on the return pass along the spine underside.

attrs.title: Materials for one leaf
attrs.body: About 8 g of DK cotton in red, orange, or gold. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Each finished maple leaf measures 9 cm across the widest point and 8 cm tall in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet".
double treble (dtr) — UK; US "treble." Used at each lobe tip.
Ch 16. Sl st into 2nd and 3rd ch from hook to form the stem. Work is now at the 4th ch — the base of the first lower lobe.

Lobe 1 (lower right): Dc. Htr. Tr. Dtr (tip). Tr. Htr. Dc. Sl st 1 (notch). Lobe 2 (mid right): Dc. Htr. Tr. Dtr (tip). Tr. Htr. Dc. Sl st 1 (notch). Lobe 3 (top/centre): Dc. Htr. Tr. Tr. Dtr (tip). Tr. Tr. Htr. Dc. 3dc to turn the leaf tip.

Along the underside of the spine, mirroring lobes 2 and 1 (left-side lobes). Sl st notch. Dc. Htr. Tr. Dtr (tip). Tr. Htr. Dc. Sl st. Dc. Htr. Tr. Dtr (tip). Tr. Htr. Dc. Sl st to the stem base. Sl st into the 2 stem chains. Fasten off.

definition.title: Maple leaf motif
definition.caption: 16ch spine. Five lobes: dtr at each tip. Centre lobe tallest. Stem sl-st at base.

content.text: Weave in ends. Steam-block flat to open the five points. Sew onto the base fabric through the outer edge.
Handwash in cool water. Re-steam-block flat after washing to restore the lobe shape.
The oak leaf (crochet-leaf-oak) uses a rounded lobe shape for contrast. Three maple leaves in red, orange, and gold together make an autumn garland panel.
